Ecal, meaning after, is a subjugating conjunction. It's never actually used to mean "after," instead being used for "if/when." There's another conjunction, which isn't subjugating, that is used for after much more often than ecal.

adam ruffled up his long coat, the fog carried a cold far into ones skin, that didnt seem to bother the universe natives on the roadside. alara was beside him, and just as unaffected as the natives. she strode on confidently, the bright reddened corset an almost eyesore in this universes blue undertones.

she batted the the words at him, as they walked "oh come now, Adam. we've worked together, but all this glamor is for the protector vigilant". Adam turned away, blushing. he looked around at the world they were now attempting to bring in as allies. the town was an imposing sight, but everywhere else there was pieces of floating stone, coursing with light like veins. collections floated as eye shaped helpers next to business-looking people. ten foot high golems dragged plows through nearby fields. and, they were assembled into stout angry looking figures that had a shield shape burning on their chest, and who eyed each traveler with suspicion.

these in particular, formed a net around them as they walked down the life-blood road to the city. adam said to alara "when we get home, should we try to bring some of these, rocks, with us" he said waving at a farming golem in the distance. she said "no luck there. they run on residual EM energy, they're just dead rocks in our universe". it was all small talk, Adam knew. they passed the threshold of the city.

decaying bodies were strung from a stone arch, with black chains and butchers hooks. more stone guards stood by the arch, for upping the intimidation factor of anyone who would watch. this was the shown price for the pairs failure on this day, and the cold was still seeping into Adams bones.
